I will keep to the crop pattern I know best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is what fits our water, our machinery, and our weather, and at my age I want a system that is steady and familiar rather than risky. Wheat gives me a reliable first harvest, and then maize follows right after, so I can use the same fields for two crops in one year. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because that makes field work, fertilizer timing, and pest control harder to manage.

For the wheat, I will carry it through the rest of the season with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and limited spraying only when needed. I will keep the field clean, watch for disease and aphids, and aim for a stable yield instead of chasing the highest possible output. After wheat harvest, I will sow summer maize quickly, using no-tillage on the wheat stubble to save labor, keep moisture, and catch the season on time. For maize I will use hybrid seed, put most of the nitrogen on it because it responds well, irrigate when the rain is not enough, and control weeds and insects with a small number of timely applications. This way I keep the work within what I can manage and stay with a system that has worked well on our plain for many years.
